findings.statement: Noon accounts for 81.9% of brand mentions in the collected sample, and its search interest shows a modest increase of 2.3% over the recent period.
limitations: Share of voice reflects the sample composition, not market share.
Trend based on search interest may not capture all user activity.

findings.statement: Arabic‑language shoppers frequently warn about fraudulent installment offers and fake WhatsApp numbers, as seen in an Instagram post that received 1,358 likes and 1,185 replies.
limitations: Based on a single high‑engagement post; may not represent broader sentiment.
Only Arabic Instagram content is captured.

findings.statement: Price sensitivity is evident, with posts promoting smartphones starting at 329 SAR and discounts up to 350 SAR, attracting strong engagement (e.g., 1,113 likes on a Facebook post).
limitations: Posts are from competitor Jarir.com, not Noon.
Price figures are promotional and may not reflect average market pricing.

findings.statement: Arabic content represents 33.9% of the collected evidence, underscoring the importance of Arabic language messaging for Middle‑East shoppers.
limitations: Language mix is derived from the sampled items, not the entire market.

findings.statement: Retailers emphasize trade‑in programs, offering up to 50% savings on new devices, suggesting a demand for flexible payment and upgrade options.
limitations: Single Facebook post from Jarir.com; may not reflect Noon’s own offerings.

findings.statement: Interest in the Noon mobile app has fallen sharply, with a 90.9% decline in the measured search metric over the last 13 weeks.
limitations: Trend based on search interest; does not capture app download or usage statistics.

findings.statement: Search interest for Amazon UAE dropped 85.7% in the same period, indicating a broader contraction in the regional e‑commerce search volume.
limitations: Reflects search interest only; may be influenced by seasonal factors.
Does not differentiate between product categories.
